# E0317: operator not defined on a type

Arithmetic works on numbers, bitwise operators on integers, and `!`, `&&` and `||` on `bool`. A string is built with interpolation, as `"Hello, {name}"`, not with `+`.

- Rule: [`expressions.left-operand-first`](../../reference/08-expressions.md#expressions.left-operand-first)
- Reported at: the operation. For a compound assignment, the assigned place; for a range, its start.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0317:1
fn greeting(name: str) -> str { "Hello, " + name }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn greeting(name: str) -> str { "Hello, {name}" }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0317_operator_not_defined_on_a_type.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0317_operator_not_defined_on_a_type.lt):

```text
── OPERATOR NOT DEFINED ON A TYPE ── E0317_operator_not_defined_on_a_type.lt:1:33  [E0317]

This operator isn't defined on `str`; build strings with interpolation, as in
"{a}{b}":

  1 │ fn greeting(name: str) -> str { "Hello, " + name }
    │                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Arithmetic works on numbers, bitwise operators on integers, and `!`, `&&` and
`||` on `bool`. A string is built with interpolation, as `"Hello, {name}"`, not
with `+`.

To fix it, build the string with interpolation:

  1 │ fn greeting(name: str) -> str { "Hello, {name}" }
    │                                         ~    ++
```
